title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
statement: You get an array `arr` of positive integers and a list `queries`, where each query `[left, right]` names a contiguous range of indices of `arr` (both ends included). For every query, combine all values `arr[left]`, `arr[left + 1]`, ..., `arr[right]` with bitwise XOR. Return an array holding these results, one per query, in the same order as `queries`.
constraints: 0 <= left <= right < arr.length for every query [left, right]
notes:
## Intuition

Answering each query by XOR-ing its range directly costs up to O(n) per query, so O(n · q) overall. XOR behaves like addition that cancels itself: `x ^ x = 0` and `x ^ 0 = x`. So if `prefix[k]` is the XOR of the first `k` values, XOR-ing `prefix[right + 1]` with `prefix[left]` cancels the shared part `arr[0..left-1]` and leaves exactly `arr[left..right]`.

## Approach

1. Build `prefix` of length `arr.length + 1` with `prefix[0] = 0`.
2. For each index `i`, set `prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] ^ arr[i]`.
3. For every query `[left, right]`, push `prefix[right + 1] ^ prefix[left]` onto `answer`.
4. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [1, 3, 4, 8]` gives `prefix = [0, 1, 2, 6, 14]` (`1`, then `1 ^ 3 = 2`, `2 ^ 4 = 6`, `6 ^ 8 = 14`).

- `[0, 1]`: `prefix[2] ^ prefix[0] = 2 ^ 0 = 2`.
- `[1, 2]`: `prefix[3] ^ prefix[1] = 6 ^ 1 = 7`.
- `[0, 3]`: `prefix[4] ^ prefix[0] = 14`.
- `[3, 3]`: `prefix[4] ^ prefix[3] = 14 ^ 6 = 8`.

The result is `[2, 7, 14, 8]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + q): one pass builds `prefix`, then each query is a single XOR.
- Space: O(n) for `prefix` (plus the O(q) output).

## Pitfalls

- The extra leading `0` in `prefix` is what makes queries starting at index 0 work; without it you need a special case.
- Use `prefix[right + 1]`, not `prefix[right]`, or you drop the last element of the range.
- Unlike sums, XOR needs `^` to "subtract"; writing `prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left]` gives wrong answers.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | `prefix[k]` is the XOR of `arr[0..k-1]` |
| `i` | index while building `prefix` |
| `left`, `right` | the ends of the current query |
| `answer` | results collected in query order |

narration.2: Make room for one more prefix value than there are elements; prefix[0] stays 0, the XOR of nothing.
narration.3: Walk through arr once to build the running XOR.
narration.4: The XOR of the first i + 1 values is the previous running XOR combined with arr[i].
narration.7: Collect one result per query, in query order.
narration.9: XOR-ing the two prefixes cancels arr[0..left-1], leaving exactly arr[left..right].
narration.11: Every query has been answered; return the results.
